claim: The C. elegans hermaphrodite gonad provides a premier system for studying organogenesis and stem cell behavior.
source: The C. elegans hermaphrodite gonad provides a premier system for studying organogenesis and stem cell behavior (reviewed by Hubbard and Greenstein, 2000; Hubbard and Schedl, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: Two gonad arms, anterior or posterior of a central uterus and vulva, are each capped by a single somatic cell, the distal tip cell (DTC), that establishes a stem cell niche.
source: Two gonad arms, anterior or posterior of a central uterus and vulva, are each capped by a single somatic cell, the distal tip cell (DTC), that establishes a stem cell niche.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge about C. elegans gonad structure.

claim: Germline stem cells and their proliferative progeny are maintained by GLP-1/Notch-mediated signaling in the germ line in response to DSL family ligands LAG-2 and APX-1 produced by the DTC.
source: Germline stem cells and their proliferative progeny, which together are referred to as progenitors, are maintained by GLP-1/Notch-mediated signaling in the germ line in response to DSL family ligands LAG-2 and APX-1 produced by the DTC (Austin and Kimble, 1987; Berry et al., 1997; Henderson et al., 1994; Nadarajan et al., 2009; Yochem and Greenwald, 1989).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Five pairs of sheath cells (named as pairs Sh1 to Sh5, distal to proximal) provide additional support to the germ line proximal to the DTC.
source: Proximal to the DTC, five pairs of sheath cells (named as pairs Sh1 to Sh5, distal to proximal) provide additional support to the germ line.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge about C. elegans gonad structure.

claim: Sh1 is implicated in promoting germline progenitor cell proliferation.
source: In particular, Sh1 is implicated in promoting germline progenitor cell proliferation (Killian and Hubbard, 2005; McCarter et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: One mechanism for the function of Sh1 cells involves the formation of gap junctions with germ cells.
source: Although the molecular and cellular mechanisms by which Sh1 promotes germline proliferation remain to be fully elucidated, it is clear that one mechanism for the function of these cells involves the formation of gap junctions with germ cells (Starich et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Invertebrate gap junctions are formed from octameric hemichannels of innexin proteins.
source: Invertebrate gap junctions are formed from octameric hemichannels of innexin proteins (Oshima et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: In C. elegans, INX-8 and INX-9 associate to form hemichannels in the hermaphrodite somatic gonad which couple to germline innexin hemichannels (INX-14 with INX-21 or INX-22) to promote germline proliferation and inhibit meiotic maturation, respectively.
source: In C. elegans, INX-8 and INX-9 associate to form hemichannels in the hermaphrodite somatic gonad which couple to germline innexin hemichannels (INX-14 with INX-21 or INX-22) to promote germline proliferation and inhibit meiotic maturation, respectively (Figure 1A–B; Starich et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research and reference to Figure 1A-B.

claim: Phenotypic analysis of reduction-of-function mutants in inx-8 recently led to the discovery of malonyl-CoA as a key cargo that traverses the soma-germline junctions to ensure proper embryogenesis.
source: Phenotypic analysis of reduction-of-function mutants in inx-8 recently led to the discovery of malonyl-CoA as a key cargo that traverses the soma-germline junctions to ensure proper embryogenesis (Starich et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The hypomorphic allele inx-14(ag17) causes Sh1 to reach almost to the distal end of the gonad.
source: Interestingly, the hypomorphic allele inx-14(ag17) (Miyata et al., 2008) causes Sh1 to reach almost to the distal end of the gonad (Starich et al., 2014) and to obliterate any bare region between the DTC and Sh1.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The hypomorphic allele inx-14(ag17) obliterates any bare region between the DTC and Sh1.
source: Interestingly, the hypomorphic allele inx-14(ag17) (Miyata et al., 2008) causes Sh1 to reach almost to the distal end of the gonad (Starich et al., 2014) and to obliterate any bare region between the DTC and Sh1.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: A loss of bare regions was observed in inx-8(0) inx-9(0) double mutants in which germline proliferation was largely restored through expression of an inx-8::gfp transgene in the DTC only.
source: Similarly, a loss of bare regions was observed in inx-8(0) inx-9(0) double mutants in which germline proliferation was largely restored through expression of an inx-8::gfp transgene in the DTC only (Starich et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: If Sh1 cannot form gap junctions with germ cells, Sh1 becomes distally mispositioned.
source: This latter result suggested that if Sh1 cannot form gap junctions with germ cells, Sh1 becomes distally mispositioned.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation in inx-8(0) inx-9(0) double mutants.

claim: The consequences of Sh1 mispositioning and the accompanying loss of the bare regions for germline stem cells have not been previously explored.
source: However, the consequences of this mispositioning and the accompanying loss of the bare regions for germline stem cells have not been previously explored.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in prior research.

claim: Gordon et al., 2020 proposed a hypothesis that Sh1 might guide an oriented and asymmetric division of stem cells, such that a daughter cell in contact with Sh1 enters the differentiation pathway while the other, in contact with the DTC, remains a stem cell.
source: The spatial relationship between the DTC, Sh1 and the germ line summarized above was recently challenged, and an hypothesis put forth that Sh1 might guide an oriented and asymmetric division of stem cells, such that a daughter cell in contact with Sh1 enters the differentiation pathway while the other, in contact with the DTC, remains a stem cell (Gordon et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a citation to a prior study's hypothesis.

claim: If oriented cell fate-determining germ cell divisions occur, the expectation would be that germ cells undergoing such a division should be in contact with both the DTC and Sh1.
source: If oriented cell fate-determining germ cell divisions occur in this way, the expectation would be that germ cells undergoing such a division should be in contact with both the DTC and Sh1, and that closely spaced daughter germ cells that have recently undergone such a division would remain in contact with one or the other.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the hypothesis proposed by Gordon et al., 2020.

claim: The model predicts that there should be few, if any, germ cells that contact neither the DTC nor Sh1.
source: The model predicts that there should be few, if any, germ cells that contact neither the DTC nor Sh1.
evidence: This is a prediction derived from the hypothesis proposed by Gordon et al., 2020.

claim: If Sh1 drives cell fate-determining germ cell divisions, altering the position of Sh1 in the distal–proximal direction should similarly alter the position of the germline stem cell fate decision.
source: If Sh1 drives cell fate-determining germ cell divisions, another expectation would be that altering the position of Sh1 in the distal–proximal direction should similarly alter the position of the germline stem cell fate decision.
evidence: This is a prediction derived from the hypothesis proposed by Gordon et al., 2020.

claim: Much of the analysis in Gordon et al., 2020 was performed using an INX-8 fusion protein marker that could conceivably alter the position of Sh1.
source: However, given that much of the analysis was performed using an INX-8 fusion protein marker that could conceivably alter the position of Sh1, and given that the precise relationship between the position of Sh1 vis-à-vis the border of the stem cell pool was not investigated, we wished to determine how hypomorphic innexin alleles alter the position of Sh1 and whether the position of Sh1 influences the border of the germline stem or progenitor pools.
evidence: This is a concern raised about the prior study's methodology.

claim: The precise relationship between the position of Sh1 vis-à-vis the border of the stem cell pool was not investigated in Gordon et al., 2020.
source: However, given that much of the analysis was performed using an INX-8 fusion protein marker that could conceivably alter the position of Sh1, and given that the precise relationship between the position of Sh1 vis-à-vis the border of the stem cell pool was not investigated, we wished to determine how hypomorphic innexin alleles alter the position of Sh1 and whether the position of Sh1 influences the border of the germline stem or progenitor pools.
evidence: This is a statement about what was not investigated in the prior study.

claim: There is natural variability in the position of the distal border of Sh1 in wild-type young adult hermaphrodites.
source: As detailed below, we found that Sh1 is somewhat variably positioned in wild-type young adult hermaphrodites.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's observations.

claim: Bare regions exist between Sh1 and the DTC, characterized by germ cells that do not contact Sh1 or the DTC.
source: We confirmed the existence of bare regions between Sh1 and the DTC, characterized by germ cells that do not contact Sh1 or the DTC.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's observations.

claim: Using bcIs39[lim-7p::CED-1::GFP] to visualize Sh1, a majority of gonads (70%) are in Class 1.
source: Using bcIs39[lim-7p::ced-1::GFP] to visualize Sh1, a transgene that produces a CED-1::GFP fusion protein that fully rescues the sheath cell function of CED-1 to engulf germ cell corpses (Zhou et al., 2001), we found that a majority of gonads (70%) are in Class 1, confirming the existence of bare regions.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the study's data.

claim: In many cases, the distance between the proximal-most DTC measurement and the distal-most Sh1 measurement exceeds 25 µm.
source: Indeed, in many cases, the distance between the proximal-most DTC measurement and the distal-most Sh1 measurement exceeds 25 µm (Figure 1G; Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the study's data, supported by figures.

claim: Using three additional Sh1 markers (and one alternate DTC marker), 50–90% of gonads fall into Class 1, while Class 2 make up the remainder.
source: Using three additional Sh1 markers (and one alternate DTC marker), we found that depending on the markers used, 50–90% of gonads fall into Class 1, while Class 2 make up the remainder (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the study's data, supported by figures.

claim: Both Class 1 and Class 2 gonads contain bare regions with spacing of germ cell nuclei such that their surrounding cell boundaries are not plausibly in contact with the DTC or Sh1.
source: We note that both Class 1 and Class 2 gonads contain bare regions with spacing of germ cell nuclei (as seen by differential interference contrast microscopy) such that their surrounding cell boundaries are not plausibly in contact with the DTC or Sh1.
evidence: This is an observation from the study's data.

claim: Class 3 gonads were not observed in any wild-type worms examined.
source: We did not observe Class 3 gonads in any wild-type worms examined.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's observations.

claim: TEM analysis of a wild-type young adult worm gonad shows germ cells that contact neither a DTC process nor filopodial extensions of Sh1, representing bare regions.
source: We observed germ cells that contact neither a DTC process (nor fragment thereof) nor filopodial extensions of Sh1, and thus represent bare regions.
evidence: This is a finding from TEM analysis.

claim: TEM analysis is consistent with the confocal analysis using cell-type-specific markers in live worms.
source: Therefore, this TEM analysis is consistent with the confocal analysis above using cell-type-specific markers in live worms, and it corroborates prior ultrastructural observations made on chemically fixed TEM preparations (Hall et al., 1999).
evidence: This is a comparison of findings from different methods.

claim: In fixed preparations, the distal edge of Sh1 was shifted nearly to the distal end of the gonad in worms bearing inx-14(ag17).
source: Previously, in fixed preparations, we observed that the distal edge of Sh1 was shifted nearly to the distal end of the gonad in worms bearing a hypomorphic mutation in the germline innexin inx-14(ag17) (Starich et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a citation to a prior observation.

claim: In inx-14(ag17), the distal border of Sh1 extends to the distal end of the gonad, well distal to the average position of the DTC processes.
source: In contrast to inx-14(+), the distal border of Sh1 in inx-14(ag17) extends to the distal end of the gonad, well distal to the average position of the DTC processes (Figure 1C–E).
evidence: This is a finding from live imaging, supported by figures.

claim: The vast majority of inx-14(ag17) gonads fall into Class 3.
source: The vast majority of inx-14(ag17) gonads fall into Class 3 (Figure 1), with consistent results from three different markers of Sh1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–E).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the study's data, supported by figures.

claim: The change in the inx-14 genotype does not significantly change average DTC mean process length or the length of the longest DTC process, but it does have a significant effect on Sh1 distal border position.
source: Although our classification scheme references Sh1 relative to DTC position, we do not attribute this gross positional alteration of Sh1 to a change in the DTC. Instead, within strains with similar markers, the change in the inx-14 genotype does not significantly change average DTC mean process length or the length of the longest DTC process, but it does have a significant effect on Sh1 distal border position (Figure 1G; Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the study's data, supported by figures.

claim: Sh1 in worms bearing inx-8(tn1513tn1555) in an otherwise null inx-9(ok1502) background is distally positioned, similar to inx-14(ag17).
source: We found that Sh1 in worms bearing one partially functional somatic gonad innexin encoded by inx-8(tn1513tn1555) in an otherwise null inx-9(ok1502) background (hereafter referred to as 'inx-8(rf)'; Starich et al., 2020) is also distally positioned, similar to inx-14(ag17) (Figure 1C–E).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's observations, supported by figures.

claim: Sh1 is positioned distally as a result of reducing the function of either germ line or somatic innexins in the distal gonad.
source: Thus, Sh1 is positioned distally as a result of reducing the function of either germ line or somatic innexins in the distal gonad.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: inx-8(qy78[mKate2::inx-8]) caused a distal shift in the position of Sh1.
source: As detailed below, we found that—like inx-14(ag17) and inx-8(rf)—inx-8(qy78[mKate2::inx-8]) caused a distal shift in the position of Sh1 (Figure 2B–F).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's observations, supported by figures.

claim: The distal shift in Sh1 position in inx-8(qy78[mKate2::inx-8]) was documented by anti-INX-8 antibody detection in otherwise unmarked strains.
source: We documented this shift both by anti-INX-8 antibody (Starich et al., 2014) detection in otherwise unmarked strains (Figure 2B–C), as well as in live imaging of marked strains (Figure 2D–F).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's observations, supported by figures.

claim: The mean distal boundary of INX-8 staining in the wild type lies at ~80 µm from the distal end of the gonad.
source: The mean distal boundary of INX-8 staining in the wild type lies at ~80 µm from the distal end of the gonad, while the mean distal boundary of INX-8 staining in worms carrying inx-8(qy78[mKate2::inx-8]) lies at ~50 µm from the distal end, and the difference between these means is significant (Figure 2B–C).

claim: The mean distal boundary of INX-8 staining in worms carrying inx-8(qy78[mKate2::inx-8]) lies at ~50 µm from the distal end.
source: The mean distal boundary of INX-8 staining in the wild type lies at ~80 µm from the distal end of the gonad, while the mean distal boundary of INX-8 staining in worms carrying inx-8(qy78[mKate2::inx-8]) lies at ~50 µm from the distal end, and the difference between these means is significant (Figure 2B–C).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the study's data, supported by figures.

source: Moreover, in 89% of wild-type gonads (n=28), the distal border of Sh1 is greater than 60 µm (~15–16 cell diameters) from the distal end of the gonad, while in 79% of inx-8(qy78[mKate2::inx-8]) gonads (n=32) the distal border of Sh1 is less than 60 µm from the distal end (Figure 2B–C).

claim: In 79% of inx-8(qy78[mKate2::inx-8]) gonads (n=32) the distal border of Sh1 is less than 60 µm from the distal end.
source: Moreover, in 89% of wild-type gonads (n=28), the distal border of Sh1 is greater than 60 µm (~15–16 cell diameters) from the distal end of the gonad, while in 79% of inx-8(qy78[mKate2::inx-8]) gonads (n=32) the distal border of Sh1 is less than 60 µm from the distal end (Figure 2B–C).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the study's data, supported by figures.

source: Using bcIs39 to visualize Sh1, no Class 3 gonads (n=27) are observed in the wild type, compared to 65% (n=26) in inx-8(qy78[mKate2::inx-8)] (Figure 2D–E).

source: The same mKate2::INX-8 fusion, independently generated in an inx-9(ok1502) null mutant background (i.e. inx-8(qy102[mKate2::inx-8]), see Materials and methods Gordon et al., 2020), was also observed to shift Sh1 distally in inx-8(qy102[mKate2::inx-8]) inx-9(ok1502) double mutants.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's observations.

claim: Loss of inx-9 alone does not significantly affect Sh1 position.
source: In contrast, loss of inx-9 alone does not significantly affect Sh1 position (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's observations, supported by figures.

source: If mKate2::INX-8 were innocuous, the inx-8(qy102[mKate2::inx-8)] allele in the absence of inx-9 (inx-9(1502)) should have had no effect on Sh1 position.
evidence: This is a logical inference about what would be expected if the fusion protein were benign.

source: First, we consistently observe a dramatic distal shift of Sh1 in inx-14(ag17) using lim-7 promoter-driven transgenes (bcIs39 and tnIs5) as well as using a functional endogenously tagged allele of the fatty acid synthase gene fasn-1, [fasn-1(av138[fasn-1::GFP])] (Figure 1D; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).

source: In over 85% of gonad arms examined (n=20 and 26, respectively), the overlap between mKate2::INX-8 and GFP was complete (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the study's data, supported by figures.

source: Nevertheless, we observe a striking distal shift of Sh1 in the inx-14 and inx-8 mutants bearing these markers.

claim: Bare regions between the Sh1 and the DTC are present in the wild type.
source: We conclude that despite variability in the exact position of the Sh1 border, and despite minor differences in transgene expression, bare regions between the Sh1 and the DTC are present in the wild type, and they are greatly diminished due to a distal shift in the position of Sh1 in worms bearing reduced inx-14 or inx-8 function or bearing the mKate2::INX-8 fusion.

claim: Bare regions are greatly diminished due to a distal shift in the position of Sh1 in worms bearing reduced inx-14 or inx-8 function or bearing the mKate2::INX-8 fusion.
source: We conclude that despite variability in the exact position of the Sh1 border, and despite minor differences in transgene expression, bare regions between the Sh1 and the DTC are present in the wild type, and they are greatly diminished due to a distal shift in the position of Sh1 in worms bearing reduced inx-14 or inx-8 function or bearing the mKate2::INX-8 fusion.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: inx-8(qy78[mKate2::inx-8]) might encode an INX-8 protein that poisons innexin complexes thereby interfering with the channel and/or adhesion functions important for Sh1 positioning.
source: Based on our observations that inx-8(qy78[mKate2::inx-8)] gonads display a distally shifted border of Sh1, we hypothesized that this allele might encode an INX-8 protein that poisons innexin complexes thereby interfering with the channel and/or adhesion functions important for Sh1 positioning.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors.

source: If this were due to a toxic effect of the mKate2::INX-8 fusion protein on gap junctions, we would predict that the distal shift of Sh1 would be dependent on the presence of the INX-8 coding region.
evidence: This is a prediction derived from the hypothesis.

claim: CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing was used to generate inx-8 null alleles in both the inx-8(qy78[mKate2::inx-8]) and wild-type genetic backgrounds.
source: To test this hypothesis, we used CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing to generate inx-8 null alleles in both the inx-8(qy78[mKate2::inx-8]) and wild-type genetic backgrounds.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method used.

claim: Deletions with identical breakpoints in the inx-8 locus were generated in both genetic backgrounds [i.e. inx-8(qy78tn2031) and inx-8(tn2034)] starting 136 bp upstream of the wild-type inx-8 ATG start codon and extending 221 bp into inx-8 exon 3.
source: We generated deletions with identical breakpoints in the inx-8 locus in both genetic backgrounds [i.e. inx-8(qy78tn2031) and inx-8(tn2034)] starting 136 bp upstream of the wild-type inx-8 ATG start codon and extending 221 bp into inx-8 exon 3 (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a description of the genetic manipulation performed, supported by figures.

claim: In the inx-8(qy78[mKate2::inx-8]) context, the deletion also removes the mKate2 moiety.
source: In the inx-8(qy78[mKate2::inx-8]) context, this deletion also removes the mKate2 moiety.
evidence: This is a description of the genetic manipulation performed.

claim: These deletions are expected to constitute inx-8 null alleles because, in addition to removing the start codon, they delete amino acids 1–349 (out of 382 amino acids), including virtually all residues essential for spanning the plasma membrane and forming a channel.
source: These deletions are expected to constitute inx-8 null alleles because, in addition to removing the start codon, they delete amino acids 1–349 (out of 382 amino acids), including virtually all residues essential for spanning the plasma membrane and forming a channel (Starich and Greenstein, 2020).
evidence: This is a prediction based on the nature of the deletion and cited knowledge.

claim: The deletion mutant inx-8(qy78tn2031) displays a significantly lower frequency of Class 3 gonads than the original inx-8(qy78[mKate2::inx-8]) allele.
source: Consistent with our hypothesis, the deletion mutant inx-8(qy78tn2031) displays a significantly lower frequency of Class 3 gonads than the original inx-8(qy78[mKate2::inx-8]) allele.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's observations.

claim: Sh1 in the inx-8(qy78tn2031) deletion mutant is positioned more proximally, and therefore, like the wild type, exhibits bare regions that are lacking in inx-8(qy78[mKate2::inx-8]) mutants.
